title: What can you say about caffeine in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for caffeine; the strongest is "Temporarily helps promote alertness and wakefulness, and helps mental performance" (moderate, 100-1,000 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "A diuretic or water pill".

supported_wordings.wording: Temporarily helps promote alertness and wakefulness, and helps mental performance.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it; FDA's 2000 rule accepts alertness wording tied to occasional fatigue or drowsiness.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older: 100-200 mg per dose, at most 1,000 mg a day (energy shots 400 mg). Above 200 mg a day, wait 3-4 hours between doses.

supported_wordings.wording: Temporarily helps reduce fatigue and supports endurance and physical performance.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it, and ODS says caffeine might improve endurance, strength and power in athletes.
supported_wordings.dose_details: As above. ODS: studies used about 2-6 mg per kg of body weight before exercise.

sources.name: NIH ODS fact sheet: Dietary Supplements for Exercise and Athletic Performance (health professional)

wordings_to_avoid.why: FDA's 2000 rule (page 1026) lists 'diuretic' among class names that imply treating disease.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: FDA final rule on structure/function statements, 65 FR 1000 (6 January 2000), page 1031
NIH ODS fact sheet: Dietary Supplements for Exercise and Athletic Performance (health professional)

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
